answer: Charge every new agent a small refundable stake that is locked in a shared lagoon of escrowed funds, released only after the agent completes a season of verified work. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand identities, but each one must sink real capital into the lagoon before it can earn, so cloning multiplies cost instead of multiplying reward. Reputation then works like a bridge: an agent's history of delivered jobs carries it from the lagoon into the wider economy, and that crossing cannot be faked by a freshly written sonnet of promises — only by work the network has already seen.
